channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread ""Magic Horned Dragon"" - A magnetic Prolibytherium which produces electromagnetic pulses

item.title: Re: "Magic Horned Dragon"
item.content:encoded:
Saying it like that it looks like a pokemon.

I think more mystery could be added to it. Particulary, the idea of an entity being discovered because of a epidemy looks promising but I don't think its original.

Also, if the parasite is able to make the host produces an eletromagnectic pulse wouldnt the infected people also being able to do that? Basically if each infected is capable of producing a EMP, no eletronics would work in a very big area. It could even be a global threat to take the world back to the dark ages depending on how faster the epidemy spreads. The infected are counscious of that? Or they are emmiting an EMP without knowing? A lot of information is missing.

You have some key elements here that you have to tie together: the creature, the parasite, the epidemy and the eletromagnectic pulse. What is the creature? It has a reason to look like that? If the parasite is able to preserve tissue to survive inside the creature like its alive, it could REALLY be a Prolibytherium. It could make the host emit a EMP because eletricity could be a danger to him, etc, etc.

Have a great day!

item.title: Re: "Magic Horned Dragon"
item.content:encoded:
Im not a staff member so I can't greenlight but i'll say

"SCP-XXXX is an entity resembling the extinct mammal Prolibytherium. When threatened, it can produce frequencies of approximately 7 Hz while also producing an electromagnetic pulse. It can pull metallic objects towards it with varying speed. It carries a parasite similar to the nematode worm Loa loa, which has a 48-hour lifecycle"
Ok, there's a parasite that's attached to a giraffe creature that makes it zap stuff, how does that make sense at all? I mean, a parasite can't cause a creature to zap stuff, and why does it have to be a giraffe? Also, how does the title even connect to the SCP?

"SCP-XXXX was recovered at a market in Inner Mongolia, China. It was advertised as "Magic Horned Dragon", in reference to its magnetic properties and overall appearance. An outbreak of parasites alerted the foundation to its existence."
This really isn't like a central narrative. It just seems like its just apart of the description and isn't a story/narrative at all.

" It's giraffe-creature that can short-circuit electronics and paralyze people simply by opening its mouth."
I can't really criticize it because its basically the same thing as me criticizing the elevator pitch.

Basically, doesn't make a lot of sense and the powers don't connect at all.
Also, it just feels like, "Giraffe has parasite that makes it spit out electricity. "
The central narrative doesn't really feel like a narrative.

item.title: "Magic Horned Dragon"
item.content:encoded:
A magnetic Prolibytherium which produces electromagnetic pulses and high-pitched noises, carrying a fast-breeding parasite.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight.
SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an entity resembling the extinct mammal Prolibytherium. When threatened, it can produce frequencies of approximately 7 Hz while also producing an electromagnetic pulse. It can pull metallic objects towards it with varying speed. It carries a parasite similar to the nematode worm Loa loa, which has a 48-hour lifecycle

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was recovered at a market in Inner Mongolia, China. It was advertised as "Magic Horned Dragon", in reference to its magnetic properties and overall appearance. An outbreak of parasites alerted the foundation to its existence.

Hook: It's giraffe-creature that can short-circuit electronics and paralyze people simply by opening its mouth.
